  "plain_name": "Wrong-length EdDSA signature accepted",
  "weakness": "When elliptic reads an EdDSA signature, it does not check that the signature has the expected length. So a signature with zero-valued bytes removed or appended is not refused for its length, and the same signature can be presented in more than one byte form (the advisory calls this signature malleability).",
  "weakness_quote": {"source": "S1", "text": "In the Elliptic package 6.5.6 for Node.js, EDDSA signature malleability occurs because there is a missing signature length check, and thus zero-valued bytes can be removed or appended."},
  "kind": "accepts_bad_signature",
  "area": "eddsa_signature_check",
  "affected": {"versions": "4.0.0 (introduced) up to and including 6.5.6 (last known affected version range: <= 6.5.6)", "quote": {"source": "S1", "text": "\"last_known_affected_version_range\": \"<= 6.5.6\""}},
  "fixed": {"version": "6.5.7", "quote": {"source": "S1", "text": "\"fixed\": \"6.5.7\""}},
  "notes": "The advisory's sentence names only 6.5.6, but the same record's version data has the line \"introduced\": \"4.0.0\", so do not read it as 6.5.6 alone. The sources describe changing an existing EdDSA signature by removing or appending zero-valued bytes; they do not describe making a signature for a message that was never signed, and they do not mention ECDSA. The code excerpts match the record: 6.5.7 adds one line that 6.5.6 lacks, which requires a signature given as an array of bytes to be exactly twice the encoding length and otherwise fails an assertion with the message 'Signature has invalid size'. The excerpts show only this constructor, not how a caller reports that failure."
